title: Is There an Economical Running Technique? A Review of Modifiable Biomechanical Factors Affecting Running Economy
claims: The review found equivocal evidence for an association between ground contact time and running economy: several studies found no relationship, some found longer contact times associated with better economy, and others found the opposite.
The review suggests that the amount of speed lost during ground contact may matter more than the contact time itself.
The review lists lower vertical oscillation among factors that appeared beneficial for running economy, but notes that only one study had specifically manipulated vertical oscillation.
The review reports that vertical oscillation changes during fatigue are small while increases in metabolic cost are large.

The review warns that recommending a general economical running technique should be approached with caution because of cross-comparisons, assessment of variables in isolation and acute-to-short-term interventions.
The review notes that female runners have lower vertical oscillation than male runners, but findings on whether females are more or less economical are conflicting.
